title: Improving the Quality of Life for Patients with Haematological Malignancies Through Virtual Reality-Based Relaxation Training
summary:
Patients with haematological malignancies often experience long hospital stays and significant psychological stress during treatment. Relaxation techniques can improve quality of life and psychological well-being; however, their use in a hospital setting is often hampered by external distractions. The use of virtual reality (VR) offers the possibility of transporting patients into pleasant, low-distraction environments, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of audio relaxation exercises.
The RELIEVE study is developing a VR-based relaxation training programme to be carried out using VR headsets. The study will investigate how feasible the relaxation training is within the day-to-day routine of a haematology-oncology ward and whether it is well received by patients. 
In addition, the study will investigate whether there is any evidence of effects on quality of life during the hospital stay, psychological distress, and mindfulness. To this end, VR-assisted relaxation training will be compared with audio-only relaxation training via headphones. Patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups and will be able to use the respective training programme independently during their hospital stay.
conditions: Distress, anxiety, depression and quality of life in patients with haematological malignancies (C81–C96).

interventions.name: Intervention involving Virtual Reality-supported, mindfulness-based relaxation training for haematology-oncology patients, for independent, ad libitum use via VR headset during their inpatient stay

Intervention involving mindfulness-based audio relaxation training for haematology-oncology patients, for independent, ad libitum use via smartphone with headphones during their inpatient stay (active control group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient with a haematological malignancy
Admitted to Tübingen University Hospital for inpatient treatment for at least 5 days during the study period
Exclusion criteria:
Oncological disorders of the central nervous system
Schizophrenia, severe depressive symptoms, substance use disorder with a period of abstinence of less than 1 month, or acute suicidal ideation
Pregnancy
Blindness or deafness, or severe hearing loss
Minors or persons lacking capacity to consent
Insufficient knowledge of German
Other medical reasons which, in the opinion of the study management or the doctors responsible, preclude participation.
Patients with non-oncological disorders of the central nervous system (e.g. migraine, epilepsy) and patients with a history of dissociative episodes will only be included following consultation with a doctor to confirm that participation is safe.
